question: Which Five-year plan is also called Mahalanobis plan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Second Five Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Second Five-Year Plan** (1956–1961) is widely referred to as the **Mahalanobis Plan**, named after the eminent Indian statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**. He was instrumental in formulating this plan and provided the framework for rapid industrialization in India.
 
• The plan emphasized the **development of the public sector** and focused on industries such as **iron and steel, heavy machinery, and heavy engineering**. It laid the foundation for modern industrialization in India.
 
• Mahalanobis utilized his mathematical and statistical expertise to create the **Mahalanobis Model**, which prioritized investments in the production of capital goods over consumer goods. This was based on the belief that developing capital goods industries would lead to long-term economic growth.
 
• The plan was aimed at achieving a **“self-reliant” economy** by reducing dependence on imports and strengthening internal industrial capabilities. It focused on creating the infrastructure needed for rapid economic growth.&l
